title: Solver self-test counts every restart's not-run publish as a 0 ms solve
claim: On the real bundle, debugger._solver_smoke's week_solve_ms spread admits 10 rows whose payload was the not-run publish (no action, solve_time_ms 0), so the self-test reports min 0 ms and n 662 where 652 solves ran.
mechanism: _apply_unsolved_payload publishes solve_time_ms 0 for a solve that never ran (the light first refresh after each restart); cycle_row copies it into payload_solve_time_ms and _solver_smoke spreads every row carrying the key, so 'did not run' and 'ran in 0 ms' are the same value.

evidence.contention_note: shared box, load1 about 22; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb solver-filter: the one-line edit in _solver_smoke's comprehension that drops a row whose payload_solve_time_ms is 0 (applied in memory by wrapping debugger.spread for that call)

metric_definition: Rows the solver self-test's week_solve_ms spread admits whose payload carried no action and solve_time_ms 0 (n_spread minus rows with a positive solve time).
phenomenon_property: A solve-time statistic over published payloads ranges only over payloads where a solve ran; the not-run payload's inert 0 is never read as a duration.

null_control.note: the synthetic week has no restart, so no not-run publish enters the spread (solver_spread_unsolved_rows=0)

reproduction_steps: Run the command on the owner's bundle: solver_spread_unsolved_rows=10, solver_week_min_ms=0, solver_week_rederived_equal=True (the recorded self-test carries the same min 0 and n 662).
Each of the 10 rows is the first row after a restart (unsolved_rows=10; 9 at a release change or 3-interval gap, the tenth after a 28 min gap with no release change).
Re-run with --perturb solver-filter: 0 rows, n 652, min about 9.8 s.
proposed_fix_scope: debugger._solver_smoke (or cycle_row omitting payload_solve_time_ms when optimization_status is not_run); one line plus a test row in tests that feeds a not-run row.
